answer: Per-identity hardware attestation resists Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a unique secret sealed in a secure element. At registration the device signs a fresh challenge with its chip-bound key, proves it runs genuine firmware, and the network rejects any certificate already enrolled. Each identity thus needs its own physical chip, so an attacker's cost scales with the number of fake accounts, much as hauling ice from a distant glacier costs more per ton than scooping slush at the wharf. Clones cannot fake hardware roots like shards of quartz.
